issue.title: [Canonical #24] General-purpose DOC capability closure and native systems
issue.body:
## Migration record — 2026-11-25

Original development mirror: https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/4. Canonical requirements and historical evidence remain at their original URLs. The new development/CI target is https://github.com/x0796666-ui/doc2; exact source history import is pending authentication. Original state: closed.

---

## Accepted under the binding minimum foundation scope — 2026-11-25

**Completed on exact revision [11e22c4](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/11e22c484a35a183ed9f77a2125afa5f22746c41).** The later binding scope refinement controls acceptance; older exhaustive driver/interrupt/library checklists below remain historical, not independent pre-#11 requirements.

- [x] Runtime-sized independent work and causal recurrence, source repair, worker parity, typed immutable values, checked slices and UTF-8. DOC-authored lexical runs, postfix emitter, tagged DAG type checker and nested heterogeneous data validation demonstrate constructive representations rather than requiring nominal records/generics before bootstrap.
- [x] Typed imported/exported native ABI, region and byte-view authority, real POSIX buffer I/O and compatible foreign function-pointer entry; checked ranges, disjointness, canonical values, volatile/atomic/fence operations and separately granted extensible native intrinsics.
- [x] Conditional and repeated native effects, per-epoch scoped cleanup, checked failure/termination and publication isolation, explicit irreversible-effect nonrollback. DOC-authored stream and bounded allocation-offset policy using authorized region extent.
- [x] Actual x86_64 freestanding QEMU boot, memory and device bytes AB; negative bounds rejection; no guest libc/OS/evaluator. Startup/linker and external target ABI are narrow platform substrate, not DOC application logic.
- [x] Source-grounded [foundation ledger](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/blob/11e22c484a35a183ed9f77a2125afa5f22746c41/docs/FOUNDATION-CLOSURE.md), native ABI/IR contracts and executable regression evidence; build and runtime boundaries distinguished.

Exact revision evidence: [CPU job](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45535169012/job/138939968173) raw logs show all 31 AOT tests passing, including native byte views, recurrence/cleanup, arena, graph checker and nested-data oracle; sanitizer/reclamation and QEMU boot markers passed. [Software WebGPU job](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45535169012/job/138940497097) raw logs show generated mesh readback, scene replay, dynamic family parity and rollback, generated WGSL cache and GPU failure boundaries. [Physical GPU job](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45535910015/job/138942322878) checked out exact SHA, verified authenticated bundle and reported 42 native signed GPU episodes and 62 DOC source cases; [artifact 14986159569](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45535910015/artifacts/14986159569) metadata matches SHA. Skipped earlier workflow is not evidence. Raw job logs and artifact metadata inspected; ZIP contents not independently unpacked in this session.

Scope limits: the Rust/C profiles are temporary and separate, not a completed independent compiler/runtime. No arbitrary asynchronous callback or retained foreign view, universal C/C++ parity, unrestricted hardware, production allocator/reclamation or universal speedup claim. Richer nominal data types/libraries, actual drivers and OS subsystems are deferred where expressible using established foundations. Unified managed values/native effect realization, independent scheduler/allocator, production no-GC/no-RC ownership and self-bootstrap are mandatory #11 implementation/revalidation obligations. #15 must reconcile all strict model properties and reopen any applicable foundational blocker discovered. Next gate: [#15 four-pass audit](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/15); freeze Rust only after that passes; then automatic authorized #11 handoff to runtime-doc/. No new self-hosting work or Rust freeze at #24 closure.

---

## Binding handoff authorization (2026-11-24)

The user explicitly authorizes starting #11 automatically immediately after #24 is closed with verified acceptance and #15's four-pass reconciliation passes on the accepted exact revision. Do not stop or request another permission check at readiness. Freeze the accepted `runtime-rust/` source in place; begin independent `runtime-doc/` implementation and continue through #11 acceptance. This supersedes historical pause/await-authorization language only, not any technical gates, safety requirements, or separate-source architecture.

---

## Binding dynamic-computation semantics — remain entirely dependency-oriented (2026-11-24)

User explicitly confirms that general-purpose expressiveness must extend DOC's natural model rather than introduce an imperative or explicitly sequential execution model. Input-dependent computation should create/expand/repair dependency graphs or equivalent dependency-aware compiled representations at runtime, including variable-sized collections, recursive derivations, data-dependent branching and recurrence. A map-like derivation over an input-sized collection must expose independent items to the automatic scheduler; true recurrence/causal dependencies and ordered effect boundaries constrain ordering naturally, not arbitrary source order. The compiler may specialize/fuse static work, use native loops or sequential machine instructions internally and choose bounded CPU/GPU execution based on readiness, cost and hardware availability; these are implementation details, not user-controlled scheduling. No ordinary programmer-authored loop order, thread count, locks, GPU placement, explicit sequential instruction stream or second imperative language required for general computation. Preserve effect authority, determinism, graph/epoch identity, invalidation, cutoff, atomic publication, automatic resource reclamation and #13 no GC/RC policy. For #24, demonstrate a runtime-sized typed dependency computation over different inputs, growth/shrink or graph repair, parallel readiness and worker-count parity, and a genuinely dependent recurrence with correct ordering. Use actual independent work on available threads and GPU where admitted/profitable; measure placement honestly, no promise of parallel speedup or that every operation can run on GPU. Do not confuse general expressive power with arbitrary imperative syntax or force artificially sequential graph traversal. This clarification narrows the previously described iteration/recursion requirement; native systems effects remain isolated and ordered by necessary dependencies.

---

## Binding scope refinement — general-purpose capability closure, not exhaustive implementation (2026-11-24)

The user explicitly narrows the pre-#11 objective: establish the smallest coherent set of language, compiler/IR and native-system primitives that lets a self-hosted DOC implementation subsequently build almost anything expressible in general-purpose systems languages such as C/C++, subject to target hardware/OS permissions and a documented safety model. Do NOT implement every feature, library, driver, OS subsystem or C++ language construct now. A missing convenient abstraction is not a blocker if it can be expressed efficiently and safely using ordinary DOC after #11. The decisive test: would implementing this capability after self-hosting require changing fundamental DOC semantics or writing a new hand-authored C/Rust/WGSL runtime algorithm because DOC lacks the means to express it? If yes, address the foundational gap now; if no, keep the library/application as later DOC work. Avoid gratuitous duplication of mature external compiler, OS, WebGPU, ABI and device interfaces.

### Audit baseline and required closure
Read exact current source, not just issue claims. At e674a759e9f8b4e86befbf0e89366d04a2fc07f4, runtime-rust/src/lib.rs Value/Type admits int(i64), bool, nat, ints, maybe_int, text; Expr is a finite scalar/list/text subset; user functions are bounded compile-time expansion with arity <=4, not arbitrary dynamic calls; imports are pure-function-only, source read effects are specialized; typed_ir.rs exports finite checked graphs, sampled facts, no general effect/ABI executable contract. Native AOT specializes this subset. These are evidence of gaps, not proof every proposed type/operator is individually mandatory. Recheck after #21.

For each item, record REQUIRED FOUNDATION / EXPRESSIBLE IN DOC / EXTERNAL PLATFORM / DEFERRED LIBRARY, explain a constructive expression or counterexample, and test real cases:
- General composition and computation: reusable typed functions/modules, input-dependent iteration or recursion with well-defined termination/resource policy, dynamically sized work and data, branching and explicit effects, sufficient expressive power for algorithms such as parser/tokenizer, symbol table, graph/type checker, compiler emitter and dynamic dependency scheduling. Do not require programmer-controlled threads or imperative syntax just to imitate C++; preserve DOC's model. Bounded finite graph unrolling alone is not enough. No arbitrary fixed compile-time arity/512-byte expansion limit as a language expressiveness requirement; justified resource limits remain.
- General structured data: a small composable typed representation (records/products, alternatives/optional results, arbitrary typed collections or demonstrably equivalent facilities), byte/text handling, indexing, conversion, fixed-width integer/bit operations, useful floating/vector arithmetic where needed by #21 or other target code. Implement missing fundamentals, not every container/matrix/string/math library. Show how heterogeneous compiler data, recursive/linked structures, dynamically growing collections and errors can be represented with safe automatic lifetimes. Generics/first-class functions/closures/recursive types are not mandatory if an adequate equivalent is proved; avoid C++ feature-list mimicry.
- Open native boundary: typed import/export ABI, native binary layouts and function calls (including an appropriate callback/event interface or equivalent), effectful system calls and safe typed data exchange, external handles, controlled address/region operations, volatile device I/O, atomics/fences with specified memory ordering where needed. Use a reusable target-intrinsic mechanism capable of expressing target-specific operations without adding a dedicated compiler feature or host-language policy per instruction/device. Define authority, unsafe/privileged boundary, resource cleanup, concurrency and non-replay semantics. Ordinary source stays free of programmer-managed allocation, lifetimes, borrowing, tracing GC and RC; privileged page/allocator/device operations are a separate system-building domain. No general unchecked pointer requirement if equivalent expressive controlled primitives suffice.
- Native/freestanding target foundation: demonstrate a configurable C/object/link target, entry point, layout/sections, native ABI, and no compulsory hosted libc/OS/evaluator dependency for a freestanding program. Tiny target-specific boot glue/linker configuration and existing toolchains permissible. A minimal actual boot/standalone execution proof (e.g. QEMU entry plus memory and one device output) is sufficient to demonstrate the boundary. Full interrupt/timer driver, DMA controller, MMU, storage, network, OS scheduler and bootloader implementations are NOT pre-#11 gates if a documented, tested extension mechanism lets them be written in DOC later. Demonstrate representative native call/memory/atomic/volatile/intrinsic capabilities; not every architecture-specific instruction. If a system operation cannot be expressed without a new hand-written host adapter beyond narrow ABI/intrinsic substrate, resolve that concrete gap.
- Compiler self-hosting feasibility: show constructive small DOC-authored algorithm/effect examples representing parsing arbitrary input, data transformation/graph work, and emitting source/bytes, with typed IR and native lowering. Establish extensibility of compiler and runtime in DOC; no complete self-hosted compiler required in #24 (that is #11). Preserve dynamic graph, recurrence, safety, and #21 generated graphics/compute semantics. Explicitly identify bootstrap circular dependencies, low-level allocation primitives and platform interfaces, so the eventual DOC-authored runtime can implement its own mechanisms, not depend on the temporary Rust evaluator.
 
### Minimum acceptance (supersedes exhaustive driver/interrupt showcase requirements below)
1. A source-grounded capability matrix with constructive examples; address actual semantic/ABI/IR gaps, document target limits and prove which higher-level facilities are implementable in DOC later. No claims of universal C/C++ feature parity, unrestricted hardware access, or arbitrary target support.
2. Small, focused end-to-end tests: nontrivial input-dependent typed algorithm over data (compiler-relevant), hosted native ABI/data/memory/effect/atomic path, and a minimal freestanding execution proof with memory and one device operation. Native compilation and actual execution, typed negative/failure/resource safety, no hidden host-side application logic. Reuse existing test harnesses. New primitive support in reference and applicable native lowering/typed IR, or clearly justified freestanding-only native semantics.
3. Exact-SHA regression evidence for #21 and existing engine/language, CPU/software/physical GPU where applicable; audit #13 memory model, build dependencies, and handoff to #11. Only foundational gaps block #24; no new app demos or exhaustive libraries. #15 reviews the combined foundation. #11 implements actual self-hosting and revalidates all accepted primitives without the original Rust/Goose evaluator. Libraries and actual OS/GPU-only research #23 remain deferred. Final #11 target is the capability to implement a broad range of C/C++-class programs in DOC, not API, performance, syntax or feature parity with either language.

Sequence remains #21 → #24 → #15 → #11. Keep #11 paused until gates pass; no automatic resumption. Record actual implementation and verification, not a theoretical completeness claim.

---

Canonical requirements: https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/24

## Objective

Make DOC a high-level general-purpose language capable of systems programming without requiring another language for system policy, runtime algorithms, OS kernels or device-driver logic. Native compilation alone does not establish these capabilities. Establish and validate the language/IR foundations before the #15 audit and #11 self-hosting migration.

**Sequence:** #21 (3D game and DOC-authored GPU kernels) → this issue → #15 (reconciliation and four-pass audit) → #11 (self-hosting). Keep #11 paused until all three prerequisite gates pass. The current Rust implementation is a temporary reference/bootstrap; implement and validate semantics there and through the available native code-generation path, then preserve them in the DOC-authored compiler/runtime in #11. Actual full operating-system development, GPU-only virtual-machine research, and hardware bring-up beyond the agreed proof remain deferred to #23 or future issues.

## Required language and system interfaces

- [ ] Typed native ABI/FFI: import/export functions, explicit calling conventions and linkage, callbacks where supported, binary layouts/alignment/padding, fixed-width integers and bit operations, arrays/records, deterministic representation, safe conversions and error propagation. Support external libraries and raw system interfaces without making C or Rust a required application-authoring language.
- [ ] Controlled address spaces and memory access: typed address/region or capability-based interfaces, bounded reads/writes, alignment, safe slicing and binary serialization, explicit device/physical/virtual address distinctions, mapping/unmapping as effects with authority and deterministic resource lifetime. Provide deliberately isolated mechanisms for genuinely privileged hardware access; no accidental arbitrary pointer dereferences in ordinary pure expressions.
- [ ] Concurrency and device synchronization: atomics, memory ordering, fences/barriers, volatile MMIO operations (distinct from atomic synchronization), safe interrupt/event and DMA boundaries, publication and ownership invariants. Document how these compose with DOC dependency scheduling and GPU operations. Privileged/ordered effects must not be speculatively replayed or treated as ordinary pure GPU computations.
- [ ] Architecture-specific operations through a minimal typed intrinsic interface: registers, privileged instructions, interrupt entry/return and control, target-specific startup and I/O as needed for a demonstrable freestanding target. Avoid an unrestricted inline-assembly requirement for normal DOC; any unavoidable target adapter must be tiny, documented and isolated from portable semantics. Do not imply commodity WebGPU exposes arbitrary GPU hardware privileges.
- [ ] Native target control: freestanding compilation without a hosted libc/OS dependency, entry points, target/ABI configuration, section placement, linker scripts or equivalent, object/static executable production, startup and exception/panic handling. Reuse existing C/backend/linker infrastructure where suitable; generated C and machine code are targets, not separately maintained DOC algorithms.
- [ ] Automatic resource lifetime and safety: preserve #13/#11's no GC, no runtime reference counting, no user lifetime annotations, no borrow checker and no manual allocation/free bookkeeping for ordinary DOC-managed values. Separate explicit OS/device operations (mapping pages, granting DMA, managing allocator/device primitives) from general-purpose application memory management; define authority, cleanup, aliasing, reentrancy, interrupt safety and failure behavior. No blanket claim that opaque external OS/library internals use no GC/RC.

## Minimum implementation and verification before #15

1. Written normative language/IR/system-effect contracts and a capability/target matrix distinguishing hosted system interfaces, freestanding interfaces, and target-specific privileged facilities. No syntax or primitive added without defined semantics and diagnostics.
2. End-to-end DOC-authored hosted systems program: native ABI calls and callbacks, binary layouts, checked memory operations, direct system-service interaction, atomic/fence behavior, reproducible positive/negative tests. Prove actual native execution and inspect binaries/disassembly/linked dependencies, not a mocked interpreter-only proof.
3. End-to-end minimal freestanding DOC-authored kernel or bare-metal harness on an agreed initial target (prefer Linux-hosted x86_64 QEMU guest for reproducibility): boots at a controlled entry point with no guest hosted OS/libc, demonstrates memory access, a hardware/virtual-device I/O effect, timer/interrupt handling, and deterministic success/failure evidence. Use only necessary architecture/boot substrate; demonstrate system policy in DOC. The host may run QEMU on a CPU. This is NOT the GPU-only operating system from #23.
4. Preserve typed IR, dependency semantics, deterministic failure/publication, safe resources and all #21 graphics/compute and CPU/GPU regression gates. Test invalid layouts/addresses, permissions/alignment, ordering and concurrency, resource cleanup, rejected unsupported targets/effects, and verify no hidden CPU emulation or host-side replacement of claimed DOC code. Record practical limits, portability and hardware-specific restrictions.
5. Commit actual implementation and reproducible CI evidence on rtu0/doc2 main, exact SHA, with source/build/runtime dependency inventory. Audit how every new primitive will lower through #11's DOC-authored compiler; no permanent Rust interpreter or separately authored host-language runtime policy in the eventual release. Do not falsely label temporary bootstrap code as self-hosted. Link concrete evidence to #15 and #11. Address blockers before closing; #15 subsequently audits the complete combined revision.

## Exclusions and dependencies

No full OS, general hardware-driver ecosystem, custom GPU ISA, native machine-code backend from scratch, or additional target-port commitment is required in this issue. Do not weaken WebGPU device admission or #21 GPU-source requirements. #23 stays future research. #14 final release remains curated text-source-only; final self-hosted release must revalidate these facilities after #11.

Implementation tracker: rtu0/doc2 main only. Keep acceptance evidence synchronized with canonical issue.
